summary: The Petitioner, VEH Jayin Renewables Private Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the Petitioner”), has filed the present Petition inter alia seeking relaxation and condonation of delay in furnishing Connectivity Bank Guarantees, namely Conn-BG1 and Conn-BG3, in terms of Regulation 37(10)(d)(ii) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2025. - _e) Pass such further order(s) and direction(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case_ . - _d) Direct CTUIL to process and execute the requisite Connectivity Agreement(s) (CONN4) and related documentation, uninfluenced by the pendency of the present Petition; and_ - _e) Pass such further interim order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ - _d) Direct CTUIL to process and execute the requisite Connectivity Agreement(s) (CONN4) and related documentation, uninfluenced by the pendency of the present Petition; and_ - _e) Pass such further interim order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case_ - **(d)** Petitioner entered into a Power Purchase Agreement with AEI New Energy Trading Private Limited for the captive supply of 150 MW capacity (“PPA”). In terms of the PPA, the Petitioner is obligated to commission the Hybrid Project within twenty (20) months from the date of execution thereof, i.e., on or before 30[th] June 2026. - **(g)** Prior to expiry of the stipulated deadline, the Petitioner informed CTUIL that it was in the process of arranging Conn-BG1 and Conn-BG3 in respect of the additional 45 MW capacity and requested a short extension of fifteen (15) working days for submission of the said Bank Guarantees. It was stated that while it acknowledges its obligation to remain apprised of regulatory developments, the communication dated 06.11.2025 was the first instance in which the requirement for submission of Conn-BG1 and Conn-BG3 pursuant to the GNA Regulations was specifically brought to its attention by CTUIL. To the extent any prior communication may have been issued, the same appears to have been addressed to a previously designated point of contact who ceased to be associated with the Petitioner Company in early November 2025. The Petitioner clarifies that the above facts are stated solely to explain the circumstances in which the delay occurred and not to attribute any lapse on account of CTUIL. - **(i)** CTUIL, in response to the Petitioner’s email dated 07.11.2025 seeking extension of time, informed the Petitioner that, in terms of the GNA Regulations, extension of the time period for submission of Bank Guarantees was not permissible. It was further stated that the requisite Bank Guarantees were required to be furnished on or before 08.11.2025, and that any Bank Guarantee submitted beyond the stipulated timeline could not be accepted. On 28.01.2026, in response to CTUIL’s communication, the Petitioner addressed a letter requesting acceptance of the Bank Guarantees submitted in respect of the additional 45 MW solar capacity. In the said letter, the Petitioner explained that the delay in the submission of Conn-BG1 and Conn-BG3 had occurred due to internal multi-tier approval processes and lender consent requirements applicable to the project, which operate under structured governance and funding mechanisms. The delay was neither intentional nor deliberate, and the Petitioner requested that the Bank Guarantees be accepted to avoid adverse - **(m)** The Petitioner relies on the consistent approach of this Commission in relaxing timelines in appropriate cases, including Order dated 22.09.2023in Petition No. 11/SM/2023 and Order dated 25.03.2025 in Petition No. 89/MP/2025, wherein delay in procedural compliances, including submission of Bank Guarantees, was condoned in cases demonstrating bona fide intent and substantial compliance. - **(n)** Accordingly, the Petitioner has prayed that this Commission exercise its powers under Regulations 41 and 42 to relax the procedural timeline, condone the delay, accept the Bank Guarantees, and protect and restore the approval granted for the additional 45 MW generation capacity in the interest of justice, equity, and public interest _._ - _(g) Accordingly, the Petitioner is also pressing for interim directions to CTUIL to permit the Petitioner to continue all commissioning and associated activities in respect of its 151.8 MW Project and the additional 45 MW Solar Project without prejudice to the rights and contentions of parties, and to process the technical data submitted by the Petitioner and issue the connection details in CONN-TD-4._ - **(d)** The Petitioner has itself acknowledged in Para 8.29 of the Petition that it sought an extension on 07.11.2025, one day before the deadline, and clarified that the delay occurred in part due to internal multi-tier approval processes and lender consent requirements. These are internal organisational constraints of the Petitioner, the management of which is entirely within the Petitioner's domain and cannot constitute grounds to override mandatory regulatory timelines. - _e) The Petitioner is also pressing for an interim direction to CTUIL to permit the Petitioner to continue all commissioning and associated activities in respect of its 151.8 MW Project and the additional 45 MW Solar Project without prejudice to the right and contention of the parties, and to process the technical data submitted by the Petitioner and issue the connection details in CONN-TD-4._ **12.** Considering the submissions made by the parties, the Commission reserved the matter for order. on similar relief granted by the Commission in earlier cases, particularly the Record of Proceedings dated 22.5.2025 in Petition No. 346/MP/2025 and in another matter.
